<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**[[U.S. Defense Secretary]] [[Mark Esper]] says that the U.S. and the [[Taliban]] have [[negotiate]]d a proposal for a seven-day reduction of violence in [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-afghanistan-talks-pentagon/u-s-taliban-have-negotiated-proposal-for-seven-day-reduction-in-violence-pentagon-chief-idUSKBN2071YX (Reuters)]
*[[Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian Civil War]]
**The [[Israeli Air Force]] launches an air raid on [[Iran]]ian targets in the [[Syria]]n capital [[Damascus]]. Syrian [[state media]] says the [[Syrian Air Defense Force|Air Defense Force]] intercepted several missiles. [https://www.jpost.com/Arab-Israeli-Conflict/Israel-strikes-Iranian-targets-near-Damascus-report-617569 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*Around two dozen heavily armed men dressed in military fatigues storm a court building in [[El Progreso]], north-western [[Honduras]], freeing Alexander Mendoza, a senior leader of the [[MS-13]] [[gang]] and killing four police officers. Honduran President [[Juan Orlando Hernández]] offers a $80,000 reward for information leading to Mendoza's recapture. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-51501103 (BBC News)]

;Arts and culture
*[[45th César Awards]]
**The entire board of [[France]]'s [[César Award]]s resigns following controversy over the [[Académie des Arts et Techniques du Cinéma|Academy]] giving [[Roman Polanski]]'s ''[[An Officer and a Spy (film)|An Officer and a Spy]]'' 12 award nominations, the most out of any film this year. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-51494929 (BBC News)]

;Business and economy
*[[United States|American]] [[newspaper]] publisher [[McClatchy]], whose assets include the ''[[Miami Herald]]'' and ''[[The Sacramento Bee]]'', files for [[Chapter 11, Title 11, United States Code|Chapter 11 bankruptcy]] protection. [https://thehill.com/homenews/media/482899-mcclatchy-nations-second-largest-newspaper-company-files-for-bankruptcy (''The Hill'')]
*[[Canada|Canadian]] airplane manufacturer [[Bombardier Inc.|Bombardier]] sells its remaining stake in the [[Airbus A220|A220]] model, previously called the C-Series, to [[France]]'s [[Airbus]], effectively closing its commercial aviation line of business. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/bombardier-financial-results-airbus-c-series-1.5462182 (CBC)]
*[[Cannabis in the United Kingdom]]
**The [[Food Standards Agency]] gives producers of [[Cannabidiol]]-related products until March 2021 to register their goods, or they will be pulled from the market. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-51480940 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mainland China]]
***[[China|Chinese]] officials report 15,152 new confirmed cases of the [[2019-nCoV acute respiratory disease]] (COVID-19) and 254 new deaths in [[mainland China]], the largest single day increase since the pandemic began. However, the number of [[Scientific method#Confirmation|confirmed]] cases now also includes the number of [[Medical diagnosis|clinically diagnosed]] patients in [[Hubei]] province. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/02/13/coronavirus-latest-updates-china-hubei.html (CNBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
***[[Japan]]'s [[Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare]] reports the country's first death related to the COVID-19 pandemic, a woman in her 80s. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2020/02/13/national/science-health/health-ministry-reports-first-death-related-covid-19-japan/#.XkVgMSOnxPZ (''The Japan Times'')]

;International relations
*[[Sudan–United States relations]]
**As part of [[government of Sudan|government]] efforts to remove the country from a [[State Sponsors of Terrorism (U.S. list)|list of State Sponsors of Terrorism]], Sudan agrees to compensate the families of sailors killed in an [[al-Qaeda]] [[USS Cole bombing|attack against the USS ''Cole'']]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sudan-usa-court/sudan-agrees-to-compensate-families-of-uss-cole-victims-state-news-agency-idUSKBN2071D1 (Reuters)]
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]]
**[[Venezuelan]] Foreign Affairs minister [[Jorge Arreaza]] announces that his government, led by [[Nicolás Maduro]], will take the U.S. to the [[International Criminal Court]] for alleged "[[crimes against humanity]]". [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/venezuela-slams-trump-for-sanctions-set-on-regime-change/2020/02/13/62a043ae-4e85-11ea-967b-e074d302c7d4_story.html (''Washington Post'')]

;Law and crime
*The [[Indonesian government]] declares that all nationals who join [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] automatically lose [[Indonesian nationality law|their citizenship]], and refuses to [[repatriate]] fighters captured in Syria. [https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/02/13/government-declares-indonesian-is-fighters-in-syria-stateless.html (''The Jakarta Post'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 British cabinet reshuffle]]
**Amid a [[cabinet of the United Kingdom|cabinet]] reshuffle by [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]], [[Sajid Javid]] resigns as the [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Chancellor of the Exchequer]] after reportedly refusing to sack his adviser team. Javid is replaced by [[Chief Secretary to the Treasury]] [[Rishi Sunak]], who becomes the first [[Hinduism in the United Kingdom|Hindu]] to hold the senior position. [https://news.sky.com/story/whos-in-and-whos-out-in-boris-johnsons-reshuffle-11932951 (Sky News)] [https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/news/politics/who-is-rishi-sunak-the-rise-and-rise-of-the-country-s-new-chancellor-1-10255242 (''The Yorkshire Post'')]
**The [[Attorney General for England and Wales]] [[Geoffrey Cox (British politician)|Geoffrey Cox]] is sacked by Johnson. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/geoffrey-cox-reshuffle-cabinet-boris-johnson-attorney-general-tory-latest-a9333076.html (''The Independent'')]
**[[Secretary of State for Northern Ireland]] [[Julian Smith (politician)|Julian Smith]], [[Secretary of State for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy|Business Secretary]] [[Andrea Leadsom]] and [[Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs|Environment Secretary]] [[Theresa Villiers]] all leave the [[government of the United Kingdom|government]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-51474171 (BBC News)]
*The [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] votes 55–45 to pass a measure requiring [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] to win approval from [[United States Congress|Congress]] before taking [[War Powers Resolution|further military actions]] against Iran. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/senate-votes-limit-trumps-war-powers-iran-200213190949919.html (Al Jazeera)]
